title: The Hash Is the Artifact: Dual-Mode Evidence Receipts with Seed-Reconstructed Originals, Anchored on the Bitcoin Blockchain
description:
SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE: AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Errors are disclosed, not erased. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All payloads synthetic or owner-authored; no customer-identifiable data appears in this record (POL-DISC-001).

Technical report formalizing seed mode for evidence receipts. Digest-only blockchain anchoring proves existence but not possession. For artifacts produced by a deterministic generator, this report closes the gap: the anchored value becomes a 32-byte generative seed from which any party can reconstruct the original byte-identically at any time — the hash is the artifact. Formalizes MHCN-3 dual-mode receipts (R11), generator pinning (R12), an information-theoretic domain-honesty rule (R13), a security-inversion rule (R14), and a seven-point pilot gate (R15). Reports two Bitcoin-anchored demonstrations (an 8,858-byte structured document and a 51,560-byte patent-citation artwork, U.S. Patent Application 19/693,343 cited publicly only), a disclosed-and-fixed first-mint rendering defect as a preregistration case study, and a public zero-trust browser examiner station where any visitor reconstructs the artifact from its published fingerprint and verifies the canonical hash locally. Extends MHCN-1 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23445938), the evidence stack (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23446098), and the Council Session 04 review (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23446655). Series No. 1 bundle: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23447609.

Dual Mesh Benchmark: MEASURED (scoped) — deterministic generators and hashes only; no neural-mesh inference in any result. Program benchmark: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23321637 (DeepSeek column: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241).

Try it: paste fingerprint 81d4a5cb97fa972e89a3b65f51076384b64d4b630291a9986bd7b067adc3456c into the public Genesis Viewer hash drop (Deterministic Coding site, linked from the Squirl OS Vault Public Links page) and verify in your own browser.
